ns2:section.sectionText: How do court decisions and precedents influence economic behavior and the efficiency of economic outcomes? The course will apply some basic microeconomic analysis to an understanding of the law. We will cover property law, contracts, torts, and the concept of crime and punishment. In each case, we'll study the economic incentives presented by the existing U.S. law and some alternatives, and analyze what provisions of the law would best facilitate market transactions and other decisions by individuals that maximize economic efficiency. To do this, we cover some welfare economics, externalities, and public goods. We will also learn just a bit of game theory and other analytical tools that are useful to evaluate existing law and reform proposals.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to Accountancy or Economics or Finance or Business Administration major(s). Not intended for students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing.
